source.stem: Which nutrient produces a purple colour when mixed with biuret solution?

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Microorganisms produce biogas from waste in an open, well-aerated heap.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Waste becomes manure on its own, which then attracts microorganisms to feed on it.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Soil microorganisms turn plastic wrappers into nutrient-rich manure.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Fresh peels blackened with soot are already nutrient-rich manure.

intelligence.enrichment: Some soil microorganisms, especially fungi and bacteria, act on plant waste and slowly break it down into simpler nutrient-rich manure. Helpful bacteria can also decompose animal waste, and some microorganisms in oxygen-free environments decompose plant and animal waste as a source of biogas. Microorganisms act on organic waste -> waste breaks down into simpler material -> manure, cleaner surroundings, or biogas can result. The learner correctly applies this rule: Some soil microorganisms, especially fungi and bacteria, act on plant waste and slowly break it down into simpler nutrient-rich manure. Helpful bacteria can also decompose animal waste, and some microorganisms in oxygen-free environments decompose plant and animal waste as a source of biogas. Peels turn into manure just because they dry out in soil; microbes are not doing the work.
